- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match true mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows rising optimism (e.g., >0.5) and price is trending up, model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for potential drop.
- Model tends to lag in early days of new sentiment shifts; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment changes sharply.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often averages out; use median of recent 5-day window instead of 30-day mean for short-term correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often overestimates volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment >0.7.
